rationale: B wins because it keeps the live wire in the frame without pretending REI should pitch it: "REI's record payout to members lands as workers organize at its stores" is exactly the risk a founder needs surfaced before walking into retail press. A is strong, but its co-op angle leans on an unproven market thesis — "The prevailing belief: resale and repair cannibalize new-product sales" — and then punts the union story as "off-beat." That is not fatal, but it is the difference between useful angles and a useful press strategy.
gaps_in_A: "The prevailing belief: resale and repair cannibalize new-product sales" imports a market assumption the update did not provide. The angle can ask that question, but it cannot build the spine of the story on it yet.

"Record dividend lands amid union drives — what REI owes its workers vs its members" is refused as "off-beat." The instinct not to pitch it proactively is right; burying it instead of making it a defensive-comment lane is too tidy.
"What an REI membership now gets you" is serviceable, but it stays national and abstract. The stronger version needs the local store, one member, one item, one price, and ideally a photo.
"journalist-fit-check ... once one angle is picked and the dividend figure is in hand" misses two gates before outreach: repair capacity by store and at least one pilot metric.
gaps_in_B: "the co-op had its best year for members" slightly overstates "largest-ever annual member dividend." Biggest payout is not automatically best year; B later knows this, but the line should not slip through.

"every store has to staff and stock" assumes operating mechanics the update does not disclose. Good angle, but phrase it as the reporting question until REI confirms on-site repair and inventory handling.
"Use `newsjack-detector` only if a current retail or resale signal appears" is a process flourish, not a press move. The real next step is proof collection and labor-response prep.
